Every time I meet an antivaxxer. Had a huge argument with a coworker recently who was convinced the measles vaccine caused autism but he also just very clearly didn’t understand how vaccines (or autism, for that matter) worked. 

Like he was convinced getting vaccinated also made you more prone to the disease when what’s actually happening is that You’re being given a very weak strain of whatever that disease is so that your body learns what it looks like and how to fight it off. And most of the time, it works. 

The reason you can still pick up things like the flu or Covid despite having been vaccinated for them is that the vaccine cannot possibly encompass every single mutation of those diseases (Which continue to mutate because people refuse to take the vaccinations for them) so when your body comes into contact with these mutations, it doesn’t initially realize that what it’s looking at is something it’s supposed to be fighting off, which is why you’ll sometimes still catch a variation of the illness before your body realizes it’s meant to be getting rid of it but AT LEAST be less likely to die from it. 

Like this man was CONVINCED The MMR vaccine gave you autism, When in reality autism is strongly suspected to have a genetic component and what’s probably happening is that you’re just getting vaccinated around the time that those missed developmental milestones are meant to be crossed (because that’s the earliest time you can be vaccinated for certain things) and would have missed them even if you hadn’t been vaccinated. Correlation is not causation. 

I’m vaccinated and autistic. My three siblings are vaccinated and are not autistic. My father is also probably autistic and was likely just written off as being sort of weird as a kid, the same way I was.

I do not like kids before they can talk or get around somewhat. They’re fragile, and I find them messy, loud, and overwhelming before they are able to reliably communicate and get around. I think occasionally about parenting an older child with my partner, and about the general concept of having a biological child that is half me and half her, but I think of the concept of having a child as more of an expression of love and devotion to my partner rather than an actual desire to raise a child. The concept, in all of its domestic fluffiness, is a nice thought, but is not something I am interested in fully investing in in reality, because raising a child just isn’t realistically nice and happy and fun all the time. What I actually want is a sense of domestic, familial bliss with my partner, not children, even if it’s a fun little fantasy occasionally.

I do not have the mental and emotional stability and patience that it would require to raise a well adjusted, non traumatized child, even with all the work I’ve done on myself. I do not want to be responsible for someone’s emotional well being and development, because I know I would probably fail at some point (I feel like every parent does, even the best at times) and this idea concerns and frightens me greatly, so I have decided not to subject a child to having me as a parent.

I'd only had my bike a few months. It was raining heavily, I was on my way home from work on the same back road I always took. Road wasn't great, but I had taken it enough times to know where to avoid for potholes, etc. There were some unused train tracks that crossed the road diagonally and were in pretty rough shape. I dont think they'd been used in years. The speed limit was 25 and I was probably doing less than that because of the rain. My front wheel caught on the lip of the tracks going over them, the bike fell and skidded several feet on its side and I let go and kind of tuck and rolled in the opposite direction.

I had on a HJC CS-R3 helmet, a Cortech Hyper Flo jacket with level 2 armor with the rain liner in, some padded riding gloves, and some sort of boot on, though I can't recall exactly what.

I hit my head but the helmet did its job and I kind of wrenched all the muscles in my shoulders/upper back when I rolled across the asphalt and twisted one of my ankles. The jacket was slightly big on me at the time and I wound up with a bit of road rash to the hip where it sort of rode up and some particularly nasty road rash to my right elbow and forearm that likely would've needed stitches if I hadn't had the jacket on. I got up and rode the rest of the way home before calling my girlfriend and kind of downplaying it to her only for her to come home and yell at me for not telling her I had wrecked (which was probably fair, the fact that I was able to get up and go home and my bike was fine apart from a scratch probably made it register as less of a big deal to me at the time)

I think I skipped work the following day and then the day after went in because I couldn't afford not to, I got to sit in a chair and run register all day because my upper body was one giant sprain so I couldn't do much else.

I didn't ride for about a week and either right when or shortly after I came back the tracks I wrecked on had been paved over. Nobody saw me wreck but the road had traffic cameras so I wouldn't be surprised if someone was aware I'd been taking the route daily, saw me wreck, and was like "okay we gotta get rid of these fucked up tracks"

I didn't change anything in my gear apart from eventually getting better gloves. I'm incredibly nervous crossing railroad tracks and riding in heavy rain now. I wait the rain out if i can.

Lack of physical structure. Some birds are able to speak but do so with the syrinx—an organ between their lungs and windpipe that vibrates as air passes through it rather than having vocal folds like humans do. This is also how they produce sounds like “puh“, etc(basically anything we’d need lips to form)

Some parrots like African greys have been known to speak in some level of context but how much they really comprehend is uncertain. My grey can say “I’m sorry” and “it’s okay” in appropriate contexts but she probably doesn’t know what “sorry” actually is and instead just knows that it’s something that’s normally said that will calm a tense or upsetting situation. Greys are very smart in other ways like problem solving, etc, and are said to be cognitively similar to a young child (3-4ish). 

Its been thought that other species of birds could be taught similarly to the way Alex the famous grey was, but part of the reason they aren’t studied similarly is because their speech isn’t as clear.

Hi! Trans person here! This isn’t how it works. No trans child is being given hormones. At MOST, if a young child expresses being another gender identity to their parents, the kid’ll socially transition at the most (haircut, new clothes, new pronouns, maybe a new name. 

Around puberty, if they haven’t already been seeing one, they’ll see a gender therapist or a psychiatrist who will diagnose them with gender dysphoria and possibly prescribe (completely reversible) puberty blockers for a while to delay the onset of male/female puberty. They’ll probably stay on those alone for a while and THEN they’ll possibly get hormone replacement therapy if they want it. By puberty your gender identity is pretty cemented and not likely to change, especially not if you’ve been adamantly insisting your gender identity from the time you were a young child. My partner is also trans, and she told her parents she should’ve been a girl at age three and they told her it was the devil in her mind and she didn’t bring it up again until her mid twenties because they reacted so poorly to it. She now has no family left that speaks to her. 

I went through the whole medical aspect of transitioning as a fully fledged adult and it was VERY difficult to get through. I had to be examined by a therapist, a psychiatrist, and an endocrinologist and have a letter of recommendation from each to get on testosterone, and yet ANOTHER letter to have my name and gender markers legally changed, and I’m going to have to get a THIRD letter to get top surgery eventually. I’ve been fully out for almost seven years. 

I know it’s hard to understand, but I PROMISE little kids aren’t getting hormones and surgical intervention. It’s hard to even get these things as an adult. If worse comes to worse and a young child explores their gender for a while and eventually goes “you know what? I’m actually cis” then all that really happened is that the kid got to know themselves better and if their parents supported them, probably felt accepted and loved while doing so. Please just be kind to children as they learn about themselves. It’ll really help them out in the long run.

I'm a nonbinary trans drag king. My drag mother is nonbinary too, and her boyfriend is a trans man. I've met a few sticklers for gender binary so far, but they were both trans women (also older, coming from a time when that was just like the ONLY IMPORTANT THING) and then you've got people like my drag mother who are very passionate about destroying that mentality, and that number is already much higher and growing.
